extracted.intended_audience: volunteer contributors assembling Sergio Aragonés marginal (marginalia) listings for Doug Gilford's Mad Cover Site
extracted.subtask_description: Compiling issue-by-issue lists of Sergio Aragonés' marginal drawings for MAD Magazine, recording brief descriptions, page numbers, within-article placement, and orientation labels; submitted items are incorporated into a chronological master list. Work is collaborative and open-ended (do one issue or many).

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer scope / workload
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do one issue. Do one hundred issues. Whatever you want to do."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors may choose their own scope; any number of complete issues is acceptable. No obligation to follow a set quantity; pick issues to compile at will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit listings only for entire issues (not partial issue selections). The project expects full-issue coverage per contributor to keep entries consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format preference
rubrics_metrics.description: "Put together a list like the examples below and email me, preferably in a spreadsheet format, but whatever works for you."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A spreadsheet is preferred for ease of integration, but other formats are acceptable. Include the same fields shown in examples (description, page, within article, orientation) to match existing entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution / compiler credit
rubrics_metrics.description: "I'll put your name below the issue list as the compiler for any issues you want to take responsibility for."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate who compiled which issues so the site will credit contributors beneath the issue listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological insertion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no real order to this.  As I get an issue, I'll insert it where it belongs in the chronological flow of things."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted issue lists will be inserted into the master chronology by the maintainer; contributors need not worry about ordering beyond specifying the issue number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description tense
rubrics_metrics.description: "When possible, try to describe things happening in the present tense."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write marginal descriptions as if the action is occurring now (present tense) to keep entries consistent and searchable. The maintainer will edit for clarity and welcomes better wording from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity vs detail guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Brevity in descriptions is a plus, but detail wins in the end for future searches (CTRL-F)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise descriptions, but include enough detail (distinctive elements, actors, objects, placement) to make entries findable via text search. Err on the side of useful specificity when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation description policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The page orientation descriptions should be simple. Don't worry about being too exact here."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide straightforward, plain-language orientation labels (e.g., top right, bottom left, center). Exact pixel accuracy or elaborate placement metadata is unnecessary; keep it simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the word 'side' for page-side vertical marginals
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use the word 'side' when the marginal runs vertically on a page side, otherwise we'll assume it runs horizonally."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a marginal runs vertically along the left or right page edge, label orientation using the word "side" (e.g., "top right side"). If not specified as a side, the default assumption is horizontal placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the word 'vertical' for non-side vertical placement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use the word 'vertical' in cases when it's not placed on a page side (happened a lot within The Lighter Side of...)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a marginal is vertical but not aligned to a page edge (e.g., runs vertically within the interior columns), use the term "vertical" to indicate that orientation (e.g., "top middle vertical").

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion policy for 'spot' illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: "In later issues, Sergio did a lot of 'spot' illustrations in the contents and letters pages. These weren't necessarily 'marginals' in the truest sense. Their inclusion will be determined on an issue by issue basis."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on a per-issue basis whether small spot illustrations (contents/letters page spots) should be counted as marginals; follow the maintainer's eventual determination for each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example structure to follow
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides repeated example rows: DESCRIPTION / PAGE / WITHIN ARTICLE / ORIENTATION (e.g., "Black cat crosses putter's path | 3 | Letters | top right side").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format each entry with at least those four fields (short description, page number, article/section name, orientation). Use the examples as a template to ensure consistency with existing listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and collaborative improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: "I will edit for clarity and I invite others to offer better descriptions if they have them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should not worry about perfect phrasing; maintainer may edit entries. Community improvements are welcomed—others can suggest clearer descriptions.
